assumptions: Both arms row simultaneously, so the exercise is bilateral.
The chest is supported on the incline bench, so the trunk stays fixed and the spine does not move.
The exertion phase is the row up: scapular retraction, elbow flexion and glenohumeral extension bringing the elbows behind the torso.

Elbow flexion and scapular retraction are the primary actions per the instructions; glenohumeral extension is included as primary because the upper arm is pulled back as the dumbbells move to the sides.
Neutral grip keeps the forearm from rotating, so no radioulnar action is listed.
Because the trunk is supported, only grip, wrist stability and shoulder position hold are listed as demands; no spinal bracing is needed.
classification_reasons: The images show a chest-supported incline dumbbell row, prone on an incline bench with both arms hanging straight at the start and both elbows flexed to bring the dumbbells to the sides at the top.
The instructions describe bilateral neutral-grip rowing with scapular retraction and elbow flexion, and the schema vocabulary can represent this.

instructions: Using a neutral grip, lean into an incline bench.
Take a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip, beginning with the arms straight. This will be your starting position.
Retract the shoulder blades and flex the elbows to row the dumbbells to your side.
Pause at the top of the motion, and then return to the starting position.
